abstract_check.evidence: Note abstract matches the primary arXiv v2 abstract; source-version metadata was checked against arXiv v2 dated 2024-04-08.

claim_checks.claim: Synthetic sparse unit-normalized item/user embeddings and random cold-start slate; item relevance dot product; sigmoid attractiveness times rank examination; Bernoulli clicks.
claim_checks.evidence: §§2–3.3; note equations and dimensional/control description align with source.

claim_checks.claim: Boredom triggers when main-topic frequency exceeds threshold over recent clicked items; two variants, with churn-and-return used in experiments.
claim_checks.evidence: §3.4 and §4.1. Note distinguishes temporary topic loss from all-vector churn, and states experiments use churn-and-return only.

claim_checks.claim: Clicked-item influence uses weighted old user vector plus mean of clicked item embeddings.
claim_checks.evidence: §3.4 gives e_u := omega e_u + (1-omega) mean(clicked embeddings), but for an empty clicked set the mean is undefined. The note’s typed pseudocode adds `if clicked.is_empty(): out = user`. Labeling this an extraction convention does not make it source-derived; it defines a new transition. Replace with an explicitly unspecified zero-click update case, while retaining the source’s denominator gap.

§3.4 says all-zero user embedding implies absence of clicks, but §3.3’s finite sigmoid yields positive attractiveness at zero relevance (e.g. alpha/(1+exp(lambda*mu)) for stated positive finite settings). Note discloses that mismatch and does not add a no-click gate.

§§4.2–4.4; values match table: L=100/S=1 or 10/nI=1000/nT=10 for main tasks; reranking L=10/S=nI=10, lambda=5/mu=.30; boredom parameters 10/5/5; influence omega=.95 where enabled; 500k RL training steps, five seeds, 25 fresh-user episodes every 50k steps. Note accurately summarizes encoder/method settings and distinguishes configured settings.

§§5.1–5.3 and Tables 3–4: single-item static oracle 100 and SAC near optimal by 200k; dynamic SAC near 70 and greedy near 50; slate embedding-quality caveat; transformer-vs-GRU partial-observation trends; uncertainty results; reranking returns (PBM 21.17/13.14, dCTR 9.28/8.97, SAC 19.01/14.82) and normalized propensity MSE .570/.915. Note preserves these as paper-specific experimental findings.

Appendix B semi-synthetic Webtoon setting and outcomes, C influence values/results, and D item-score result are covered or appropriately summarized at note’s level; note states scope limitations without claiming real-world validation.

bibliography_check.evidence: The source bibliography has 55 entries; note contains 55 title-bearing links, and checked titles/order against primary HTML blocks. Existing target mappings or natural title labels are used; no opaque ID placeholders or count mismatch observed.

metadata_check.evidence: The primary is arXiv:2311.16586v2 dated 2024-04-08; source DOI and corrected title/authors are consistent with note metadata.

unresolved_or_conflicting_source_details: Clicked-item mean is undefined when the click set is empty; source does not specify a fallback/update behavior.

The churn explanation says all-zero embedding entails no clicks, but the finite sigmoid and positive alpha yield nonzero click probability at zero relevance; this source-internal inconsistency is correctly disclosed.
Composition of simultaneous boredom and influence and timer reset semantics are not fully specified; note discloses these gaps.

claim_checks.evidence: Although the adjacent prose now says the zero-click case is unspecified, the pseudocode still explicitly contains `if clicked.is_empty(): out = user`. That is an invented unchanged-user transition and conflicts with the stated disclosure. Remove that branch and leave the empty-set transition explicitly undefined/unspecified; retain the denominator gap.
